title.narrative: Gender-sensitive Humanitarian Assistance in WASH & Protection for the Rohingya Refugee and Host in Teknaf, Coxs Bazar BC

description.narrative: Bangladesh shelters over 967,000 Rohingya refugees in some of the world's largest and most densely populated camps. Six years after their forced displacement, safe repatriation to Myanmar remains unlikely due to the ongoing situation in Rakhine State. Since 2018,WHH funded by the AA, has provided WASH services in camps 24, 25, and 27, as well as to host communities. WHH now proposes a project focusing on gender-sensitive humanitarian assistance in WASH and protection for both Rohingya and host communities, aligning with Inter Sectro Cooperation Group's ( ISCG's) strategic goals. The project aims to reduce suffering, create a secure environment, and enhance social cohesion through gender-friendly WASH infrastructure, hygiene practices, and community mechanisms. Local partners will implement the project, with WHH overseeing monitoring, regulatory compliance, and technical guidance. The project targets 43,250 direct and 172,350 indirect participants from camps 24, 25, 27, Bhasan Char, and host communities in the Nhila Union.
Project Outcome:Alleviate suffering and establish a secure environment for conflict-affected Rohingya refugees and host communities by implementing essential life-saving WASH and protection services

The project aims to reach 51,632 direct participants (10,641 households), primarily focusing on Rohingya refugees (88%). The adjacent host community in Nhila Union will account for the remaining participants. The Bangladesh government recommends the provision of project services to the adjacent host communities alongside the refugees.
